# ON DIVINE NUMBERS.

...they called the **number of justice**, because it is divided into "even-even" numbers, namely into four (which is its square), and again four into twice two, and finally two is divided into two units. Because of this equality of division all the way down to the unit, it claimed the name of justice for itself. It is also called the **number of blessedness**, because it pertains to eternity and the completion of the world; because it follows the seven, which is the symbol of time <note>In this cosmological system, seven represents the temporal world of the planets, while eight represents the eternal realm beyond them.</note>. Christ also teaches as many degrees of blessedness in Matthew <note>A reference to the eight Beatitudes in the Gospel of Matthew 5:3–12.</note>. Finally, it is called the **number of salvation and preservation**.

As the harmony of the *Diapason* <note>original: "Diapason"; the musical interval of an octave, used here to represent the perfect harmony of the number eight.</note> resounded through the world from this radical and sacrosanct number, the Word descended into the formless world to give it shape, to strip away its horrifying impurities, and to drive back its foulest shadows to the center. Thus, having made a downward penetration, this wisdom of the Father—this Demogorgon <note>A primordial deity often associated in Renaissance thought with the mysterious, creative soul of nature.</note> who is one and three, or this "halfway point" of the trinity—perceived and noticed that Chaos, or rather *Hyle* <note>original: "hylam"; a Greek term for the "raw matter" of the universe before it is given form.</note>, or prime matter, existed as something formless, impregnated by potential alone and "pregnant," ready to give birth to something from nothing without the help of Demogorgon, and to bring it into reality. For its belly, veiled in darkness, trembled; the limbs of Hyle were agitated by the disturbance of its litigious birth. For unity in potentiality struggled to see action and to gaze upon it face to face. The only-begotten offspring of Demogorgon took pity on this chaos of pain, and kindly stretched out its right hand toward its laborious struggle of giving birth. Thus, as action met with potential, the firstborn of Hyle or son of Chaos—potential unity—was brought forth into action as **Strife** <note>original: "Litigium"; personified here as a primordial force of division or discord, often identified with a fallen, prideful spirit.</note> and the seed of discord. 

As soon as he had drawn the rays of life to himself from the Word or Demogorgon, this author of sedition and prince of darkness (forgetting the benefits of his creator) immediately rose up, elated by pride and ambition, and did not hesitate to usurp the place and dignity of the supersubstantial unity. He refused to admit a superior; he wanted no one to be preferred above him in eternity or power, and dared to claim the first place in the world for himself. And so this second companion, full of malice, ambition, and sedition—having gathered and assisted himself with his moist comrades clinging to him (leaping forth with him from the abyss of Hyle)—flew hostilely upward toward the formal world on borrowed wings, made from the rays of the clear fountain expanded everywhere through the moist nature in the empyrean region by the presence of the Word and the Holy Spirit. But, being ignorant of the power of the supersubstantial essence (which is incomprehensible before contact and effect), this rebellious traitor was cast down from the formal world by a single stroke of lightning and by the mere utterance of the Word. He was submerged again into the abyss of darkness with his companions and cohorts, and finally driven to the center of the material world. 

Immediately after his casting down, the universal moist nature—the second offspring of Hyle—was brought forth, whom the poets have imagined to be **Pan**. By his long beard, they understood the rays of light and the sun; by his eye-patterned head, the firmament filled with fixed stars; and by his pipe made of seven reeds, they signified the powers and harmony of the seven planets. From these things, therefore, it is clear that **Strife** was nothing at all before the presence of the Word and the appearance of the spiritual splendor, except for unity in potential. This unity could not exist in action, because that actual and formal Unity preceded it in the sacrosanct Trinity, which was its beginning; consequently, it was something "second," insofar as it proceeded from the pre-existing unity. 

The same reasoning applies to the production of universal spiritual matter, which succeeded Strife in material birth, since it is of the same genus and nature, except that its filth, impurity, and darkness are stripped off and set aside. By the virtue of the divine rays and splendor, this universal matter is made like clear water, balanced by number, weight, and measure, and rendered more obedient to its creator. Hence it is established (*to use the words of Hermes Trismegistus* <note>original: "M. Trismeg."; the legendary Egyptian sage associated with the Hermetic texts.</note>) that since the Mind, the Word, and the moist nature (which shone out from the shadow) are younger, it therefore occupies the place of the **material binary number** <note>original: "numeri binarii materialis"; the number two, representing the first step into material division and duality.</note>...

# TRACTATE I. SECTION I. BOOK I.

...this duality <note>The "Binary" or the number two.</note> is not of the same nature as that formal duality which we demonstrated above to be most complete and perfect in its essence, and the preserver of all things. On the contrary, a material spirit can no more exist in the nature of things without divine rays and assistance than a "cipher" <note>The number zero.</note> can exist without a digit for mathematicians, as was shown previously. Furthermore, this material number is in itself a number of sedition and the origin of discord; consequently, it is most imperfect, insofar as it does not possess an actual principle that is consubstantial <note>Sharing the same substance or essence.</note> with itself. Indeed, its consubstantial principle was a certain "One" in potentiality; but after it was produced into action, it abandoned that name and took on the form of plurality, losing its unity and rightly attributing that unity to the formal unit. 

And hence it is that it least possesses the unity suited to its nature in act; wherefore it has neither beginning, middle, nor end. From this, it follows that matter itself is a most wretched thing without the presence of the divine number and the assistance of the source—namely, of all goodness. For unless the <term>supersubstantial trinity</term><note>A divine unity that exists beyond the physical substance of the world.</note> flowed something of its perfection and goodness into this worldly matter, it would be nothing but a heap of evils, a gathering of envy, an accumulation of discord, an abyss of deformity, and an inclination toward the multitude. Nor would even all these things exist, except as mere potentiality, insofar as every act (as has been said) and every goodness comes from the luminous source. 

Hence, therefore, this material binary number is called the ***number of discord, confusion, misfortune, and impurity.*** And this was also why ***St. Jerome, writing against Jovinian, said that on the second day of the creation of the world it was not said: "And God saw that it was good,"*** <note>original: "Et vidit DEUS quod esset bonum." Jerome noted that in Genesis, the blessing "it was good" is omitted on the second day, which he interpreted as a sign that the number two represents division from the Divine One.</note> ***because the binary number of the world is evil.*** Furthermore, this was why ***God commanded the unclean animals to enter the ark in pairs*** <note>original: "numero binario"; by the number two.</note>, because the binary number is the number of impurity and most unhappy in its omens. Finally, this was the reason why the ***Pythagoreans*** (as ***Plutarch*** recounts) called the unit ***Apollo*** or ***God***, but called the <term>dyad</term><note>The number two.</note> ***"strife"*** and ***"audacity,"*** and applied the <term>triad</term><note>The number three.</note> to justice, which is the highest perfection. 

By the progression from this unlucky material number, which tends downward, the divine soul is imprisoned more and more, and is entangled in the densest snares of darkness, and is rendered most unhappy; it is vexed by passions and deceived by the tricks and illusions of the world. Whence it happens that the more the light descends from the view of the luminous source toward the base of the material <term>pyramid</term><note>In this cosmology, the universe is often envisioned as two interlocking pyramids: one of Light (descending from God) and one of Matter (ascending from the earth).</note>, the more it is endangered and submerged in darkness. Thus, this duality, having followed, produces the four elements, which first fortify the soul within their spirit with their viscosity; and again, plunging even deeper into its depths, the soul—captured by the snares of the spirit—is reduced even to the <term>cube</term><note>The "cube" represents the three-dimensional physical body and the finality of material form.</note>. It is introduced into the opaque body—whether we call it the three dimensions, the "elemented" of the elements, or the composition of the four elements constituting the cube of a square—by the flatteries of the spirit that belongs to the side of matter. 

And this is the reason why men are more affected by the world, the flesh, the devil, and inferior, deceptive, and vain delights than by supercelestial and divine things imbued with truth; namely, because the spirit existing on the side of matter neglects the mind and the soul and clings to the animal or elementary soul. 

But truly, pay attention and wait, O children of the earth; listen, I say, creatures imbued with divine reason; rejoice, O men, or be filled with no small joy. For all that which matter has plotted by betrayal against your souls—by sowing its discord, beginning from its duality and progressing to the universality and depth of its mass toward the center of the base of its pyramid—all that, I say, the supersubstantial duality (which is unity and trinity) shall dissolve. Through its harmony, moving in reverse through those same degrees of discord, and fixed to the formal world, it will ascend and rise from the cone of its formal pyramid toward its base; it will free the captured souls from the darkness and finally exalt them to their own natural seat. For the root in the cone of the formal pyramid (situated near the earth or the base of the material pyramid) will untie the bonds...

For just as dark matter acts to captivate souls by reducing unity into a multitude, so also God and "form" act toward their liberation from captivity by leading them back from multitude to simplicity and unity. ### CHAPTER VIII.

->*Concerning the property of the number three in the Trinity, or the third person*<-
->*in the construction of the world.*<-

This odd number <note>The "Ternary" or number three.</note> is **supersubstantial** <note>Existing beyond or above the level of physical substance.</note> and most holy, in which God is said to rejoice. Insofar as it is an uncomposed, sacred, most powerful, and most perfect number, it comprehends many mysteries of the Deity and produced many secrets in the composition of the world. For first of all, since God is referred to by the number three, it is argued and indicated that this number is the most perfect, for it is the beauty that perfects the beginning, the middle, and the end, and possesses these things as absolute equals. Other numbers that have those three degrees of perfection do not possess them absolutely and simply, but relatively and in a composite way. Therefore, this Ternary brings forth God as the beginning, cause, and form from the "Primary Form" <note>The Father.</note>; it brings forth the most perfect from the beginning, middle, and end—as the one *through* whom all things exist, and as the end *in* which all things exist. From these things, it is clear that this number is the most profound and admirable communion and indissoluble bond of the Third Person in the Trinity, clearly explaining the connection with the First and Second, and connecting all three together in an ineffable knot of unity and the same inviolable bond. ...will extinguish the poison of darkness and death; and for the first time, through a wondrous dissolution <note>original: "resolutione"; here referring to the chemical or spiritual breaking down of a substance into its parts.</note> within itself, it will reduce the material cube <note>In this mystical system, the "cube" or the number four represents the solid, physical world of the four elements.</note>—after the body’s breakdown into the four elements—refining it. It will then exalt the soul into the region of the formal square <note>The "square" represents a higher, more stable spiritual reality than the material cube.</note>, or the sphere of the sun, or the seat of equality, or the point, or the center where the two pyramids intersect <note>A reference to the "Pyramid of Light" descending from God and the "Pyramid of Matter" ascending from the earth; their intersection is the place of the soul's balance.</note>. At this stage, the soul will still be held by the snares of the four elements, nor will it be totally freed from its chains along with the mind. For this reason, the formal root will still strive toward the dissolution of the material square, and so, by dividing the quaternary number of the elements within itself, it will labor to free the soul entirely from its material snares and exalt it into the formal region with eternal blessedness.

Exult, I say! For such is the immense power of the Second Person in the Trinity, and of such great efficacy. This is His kindly nature, whose effort is always directed toward the liberation of the souls of holy men, so that they are not submerged in darkness forever. This is the only salvation for humanity; here is the Savior, the Redeemer, and the only mediator for them. And this is that expectation of our exaltation through the faith we have from Christ JESUS, the Word of GOD, who is the only leader and the sole root, conducting us from death and darkness to the illumination of the soul—which was once immersed in gloom—and to the peak of eternal life. Therefore, regarding this material cube, a saying was cast forth by Hermes Trismegistus <note>original: "Mercurio Trismegisto"; the legendary Hellenistic figure to whom many mystical and alchemical texts were attributed.</note>: *Whatever is generated is surely imperfect, divisible, increasing, and decreasing.* And here it must be noted and observed most diligently and zealously, that every increase of the body comes from matter, while its decrease comes from form and from God. For just as dark matter acts to captivate souls by reducing unity into a multitude; so also GOD and "form" <note>The spiritual essence or blueprint of a thing.</note> act toward their liberation from captivity, leading them back from multitude to simplicity and unity. From these things, the words of the Wise Man should also be carefully considered:

<margin>Wisdom 9.</margin>
> For the corruptible body burdens the soul, and the earthly dwelling presses down the mind that muses upon many things; and we hardly guess aright at things that are upon earth, and with labor do we find the things that are before us: but the things that are in heaven, who hath searched out, except thou give wisdom... <note>original: "Corpus quod corrumptur, aggravat animam..." quoting Wisdom of Solomon 9:15-17.</note>

etc. For by its life-giving virtue, regeneration occurs in this life, and in its spirit, the resurrection to eternal life.

### CHAPTER VIII.
### *On the property of the ternary number <note>The number three.</note> in the Trinity, or the third person in the construction of the world.*

This odd number is "supersubstantial" <note>A term for God meaning "above all substance" or "beyond being."</note> and most holy, in which GOD is said to rejoice. Inasmuch as it is an uncomposed, sacred, most powerful, and most perfect number, it encompasses many mysteries of the Godhead and has produced many secrets in the composition of the world. For first of all, since GOD is referred to by the ternary number, it is argued and indicated that this number is the most perfect, since it is the beauty that perfects the beginning, the middle, and the end, and possesses these things as absolute equals. Other numbers that have those three degrees of perfection possess them not absolutely and simply, but relatively and compositely. Therefore, this ternary number brings forth God as the beginning, cause, and form from the primary Form; it brings forth the most perfect thing from the beginning, middle, and end—as the one *through* whom all things exist, and the end *in* whom all things exist. From this, it is clear that this number is the most profound and wondrous communion and indissoluble bond of the Third Person in the Trinity. It clearly explains the connection with the First and Second Persons, joining all three together in an ineffable knot of unity and an inviolable bond. Therefore, the office of this Holy Spirit, or the Third Person in the Trinity, is occupied...

...concerning the perfection of the first two operations: for the breathing spirits <note>original: "Spiritus spiratores"; refers to the Holy Spirit's role in "breathing" life or proceeding from the Godhead.</note> always accompany them in their actions. Therefore, from the Father—or Unity—comes the command to build the world, and this is done through the Son. For the Creator fashioned the world by the Word <note>original: "Verbum"; the second person of the Trinity.</note> and not by hands, and this was in the power of the Holy Spirit, who was "carried over the waters." *David* seems to confess all of this in very few words when he says: *By the word of the Lord the heavens were made firm, and all their power by the breath of his mouth.* <note>Psalm 33:6. The author uses this to show the Father, Word, and Spirit working together.</note> According to the nature of this number <note>The number three.</note>, the world is divided into three heavens: the *Empyrean*, the *Aetherial*, and the *Elementary*. Their matter takes on a different character based on the fiery power or the loving glow of the Spirit of the Lord that moved over the waters. The more intense and superior power of this virtue, refining the moist spirit <note>original: "spiritum humidum"; in this cosmology, the "moist spirit" is the raw material of creation.</note> of the upper world-region to an excellent degree, rendered it entirely fiery through the fullness of its glow and heat. For this reason, it was called the "light created on the first day," and the region containing it was called the *Empyrean* from *Pyros* (which is Greek for "fire"), in which there are three parts of light for every one part of moist spirit. Furthermore, by the rays and more moderate power of this virtue, the middle region was forged, where two portions of matter equal two portions of light; hence it is called the *Aether*, for this middle region is like *Aeth-aër*, which is to say, "fiery air." Then, the fiery faculty of the divine spirit, penetrating further downward (but at an even more moderate degree), left three parts of material spirit for every one part of light in the elementary region. Again, each of these heavens is subdivided according to the order of the Triad: the upper is divided into the three hierarchies of angels, which are again distinguished into three circles belonging to each hierarchy; the middle is divided into three types of spheres, each of which is subdivided into three circles—namely, the first mover, the starry heaven, and the sphere of Saturn; in the second rank, the spheres of Jupiter, Mars, and the Sun; and in the lowest series, the spheres of Venus, Mercury, and the Moon. The lowest heaven is distributed into the element of fire, the sphere of moisture, and the element of earth; and again, the element of fire is divided into an aetherial part, an elementary part, and the highest region of the air; then the two lower regions of the air and the sphere of water; and finally, the two remaining elements are divided and distinguished into three regions of earth. This third person also works specifically within man, since his internal being is established according to the idea of the Holy Trinity—namely, consisting of mind, spirit, and soul; his external being from bones, flesh, and veins; and from the head, chest, and belly. This divine spirit also works to distinguish the types of earthly creatures, dividing them into animals, vegetables, and minerals. Finally, in the highest heaven, he causes the types of living beings to differ, distinguishing them into various natures: into gods, demons, heroes, and souls (according to the opinion of *Iamblichus* <note>Iamblichus (c. 245–325 AD) was a Neoplatonist philosopher who influenced Western mysticism with his complex hierarchies of spiritual beings.</note>), and so on in infinite other things.

We will perceive that these agree in everything (and by a direct path) with the three Persons of the Trinity. For in the superior hierarchy, called the *Epiphany* <note>original: "Epiphania"; used here to mean "appearance" or "manifestation" of the divine.</note>, the property of the Father is found, since this hierarchy is occupied with the burning...

...love and affection in the summit of the highest motion and in the weighing or liberation of particular judgments. From this, the hierarchy is divided into orders that naturally suit such properties. For the **Seraphim** (which is the superior order of this hierarchy) consist of a multitude of angels whose nature is to understand the loftiest things and to be set ablaze by the essential fire of God, inasmuch as they are nearest to the formal world and closest to the most simple dwelling place of God. The **Cherubim** are filled with wisdom and knowledge. And the **Thrones** are most fully replete with divine judgment; for (as *Isidore* <note>Isidore of Seville (c. 560–636 AD), a theologian and scholar whose works were standard textbooks in the Middle Ages and Renaissance.</note> testifies) God sits upon them in His judgment and disposes all things through them. Hence, this hierarchy is rightly attributed to God the Father.

The second and middle hierarchy is called **Epiphonomia** <note>original: "Epiphonomia". A term likely meaning "manifestation of sound" or "divine splendor."</note>, which signifies divine splendor and clarity with reverence, divided into **Principalities**, **Powers**, and **Dominions**. Thus the second person, who is the Word, is called the light of the world and the life of things, which we must especially revere as the actualizing force of things.

The third and lowest hierarchy is called **Ephionia** <note>original: "Ephionia". Likely referring to the hierarchy closest to the material world.</note>, as if pertaining to the virtues, because the spirits of this hierarchy—whether they be **Virtues**, **Archangels**, or **Angels**—have the power of performing miracles, curing diseases of both the soul and the body (and this beyond the reasoning of nature), and demonstrating mysteries. To this hierarchy the third person [the Holy Spirit] is referred, since all virtues are attributed to the world by the Spirit from the mouth of the Lord.

From the first hierarchy, therefore, as if from a source or a luminous center, the second proceeds like splendor and light from a fiery body; and just as color arises from light, so the virtues arise from the splendor of light. The first hierarchy is thus like a fiery heat, the second is divine clarity (as if from that fiery heat), and the third is a secret virtue, like the warmth from both—namely, from the fire and the light. How most manifest, therefore, do we see here the agreement of the first heaven and its parts with the Trinity.

Leaping forward from this heaven into the second, we shall also find there the Trinity under the same relationship most evidently. For in its first and supreme triplicity, embracing the **first mover** <term>Primum Mobile: The outermost sphere in classical astronomy that moves all the inner spheres.</term>, the **starry heaven**, and the **sphere of Saturn**, we perceive the property of unity and of the Father. For as unity is the first number from which the other numbers arise, so all lower things are moved by the power of the first mover. Similarly, as the firmament is called the heaven composed of fixed stars, so the Father is fixed in His nature, immovable and in no way to be altered, as is observed in the nature of unity. Finally, as **Saturn** was called the father of the other gods among the Poets, so from the supersubstantial unity or Father, the two other persons of the Trinity—the Son and the Holy Spirit—are propagated.

Again, the second and middle triplicity of this heaven is compared to the second person of the Trinity in its disposition. For as **Jupiter** was the son of **Saturn**, so the second person is the Son of the first. As he is called the "father of lightnings" (carrying lightning-bolts with him), so also is this the voice of the Father going forth with lightning and thunder, and being sent forth from the mouth of the Father with immense strengths and ineffable power, striking where He wills. **Jupiter** is also esteemed for justice, benevolence, religion, piety, as a preserver and friend of the human race, and a distributor of the radical moisture and innate heat which most easily separates things toward life. Infinite passages of the Holy Scriptures have clearly explained the Son's incomparable power, justice, kindness, religion, piety, affability toward the human race, and His operation toward life and its preservation.

**Mars**, also found in the same triplicity, proves the power and victory of the Son against the prince of impiety and his followers—namely, the crowd of iniquity—whose role it is to overcome the beast, the false prophet, hell <note>original: "orcum", referring to the underworld or the abyss.</note>, and death itself.

Finally, this second most holy person is appropriated to the **Sun** in many ways. For just as mundane harmony is said to flow from **Apollo**, so in truth from the Son (or the duality with His Spirit) is derived the universal symphony of matter—in the **Fourth** <term>Diateſſaron: A musical interval of a fourth.</term>, the **Fifth** <term>Diapente: A musical interval of a fifth.</term>, and consequently in the **Octave** <term>Diapaſon: A musical interval of an octave, which combines the fourth and fifth.</term>, which is composed of those two—as was declared above. The **Sun** is also, according to *Hermes Trismegistus* <note>The legendary Egyptian sage and purported author of the Hermetic Corpus.</note>, the son of the material world, and according to *Plato*, the image of God...

...a mortal son is visible, it is said, just as the second person is the son of the invisible God: The **Sun**, the light of the visible world, is the son of the father, the invisible light, giving essence to every creature. The **Sun** is said to pour lives into lower things every year for the purpose of generation, but the second person of the Godhead gave life and form <note>original: "speciem"</note> to things in the creation; indeed, he even established the sun itself in the heavens, so that it might pour out its property by its office into lower things, both to preserve those lives by generation in corruptible things and to retain them in incorruptible things—which that divine Word, or the second person, impressed and engraved upon creatures in the beginning. 

Finally, the lowest triplicity of this heaven corresponds to the third person of creation: For **Venus** has dominion over the moist and warm nature of the lower liquid—namely, the aerial nature; **Mercury** is the ruler of winds, breaths, and spirits (as the Astrologers testify); and the **Moon** is the mistress of waters and cold humors. Thus also from many places in the holy scriptures, we shall find the Spirit referred to the waters, the sea, the sounding waves, wine, breath, and wind; thus it is also said to *be moved in the beginning over the waters, etc.* 

If, finally, we proceed to the contemplation of the elementary heaven and make a diligent inquiry there, we will perceive that in its three triplicities, the three properties of the persons of the individual Trinity are found in their own proper order. For the fiery triplicity is referred to the first person; it is the highest element, most subtle, most pure, most powerful, most active, and living—as it were, the storehouse and treasury of the lower light. Thus the first person is the father of the universal light, the highest, most simple, most powerful, and swiftest in action. Again, this fiery element consumes and destroys all lower impure things; so it is also said that **GOD** is a consuming fire, <note>A reference to Deuteronomy 4:24 and Hebrews 12:29.</note> and so subtle, penetrating, and effective, that no mortal can see Him in His essence and live. 

The properties of the second person are also found in the triplicity of the sphere of humidity, namely, the air. For just as air is immediately from fire (indeed, it is the very spirit of fire, formed from two parts of fire no differently than a duality is formed from two units), so in this it is compared to the second person proceeding from the fiery and loving father. Furthermore, as air is the administrator of life in passive things, so is the second person, or the Word, in active things. Whence **Hermes Trismegistus** <note>A legendary Hellenistic figure, often identified with the Egyptian god Thoth, regarded as the source of ancient wisdom and alchemy.</note> says: *The Word standing by the moist nature cherished it, etc.* 

There is, therefore, a vital light in the spirit, and an innate heat in the air, which has a relationship to the rays of Jupiter in the consonance of the **Octave** <term>Diapason</term> <note>The Greek term for an octave, used here to suggest a harmonic, musical relationship between the celestial and elemental realms.</note>; and consequently, every superior property of any heaven responds to the property of a lower heaven, as will appear most evidently once a proper inquiry is made. Finally, the third person has a relationship to the air as well as to the water, the spirit, and the winds enclosed in the earth, for the reasons alleged above. There is also another threefold relationship of property described by the **Prophet Amos** in these words:

> *He who builds his ascension in heaven, who founds his bundle upon the earth, who calls the waters of the sea and pours them out upon the face of the earth.*

And again by the **Prophet Jeremiah**, in these words, in the same sense and similar order as the aforementioned Prophet:

> *He who gives the sun for light by day, the order of the moon and stars for light by night, who stirs the sea, and its waves roar; the Lord of hosts is his name.*

And by the **Prophet Joel** in these words, not in a different sense, but in a different order: *The floors shall be full of wheat, and the presses shall overflow with wine and oil.* In **Amos** and **Jeremiah**, the order is one, but reversed and changed for the distinction of necessary operation; but in **Joel**, it is mixed. **Abbot Odo** <note>Likely Odo of Cluny (c. 878–942), a major figure in the Cluniac Reforms and a writer on music and theology.</note> seems to open the understanding of these passages to us in this way, interpreting them thus: *The Spirit, who calls the waters, stirs the sea, and fills the presses with wine; the Son, who founds the bundle upon the earth, gives the order of the moon and stars, and fills the floors with wheat; the Father, who builds the ascension, gives the sun, and fills the presses with oil, etc.* Because oil is conferred by property to the Father, who is kind, since it is a balm soothing all wounds and taking away pains; the bundle of wheat nourishes all, like the Son; and the Spirit administers life.

# ON DIVINE NUMBERS.

## CHAPTER 10.

->*Concerning the reason according to Mathematics <note>original: "Mathesin"</note>: first, why the Deity is designated by number, and then why by the triad; similarly, why according to the Logicians, relation is attributed to the Deity.*<-

Now indeed, we have proposed to bring these reasons into the public view: first, why Theology has dedicated God to **number**, and then we shall bring forward geometric reasons why she chose the **triad** <note>original: "numerum ternarium," the number three</note>—the creator and form of all things—to express God, and dedicated the Deity to such a number. First, therefore, it must be known that Divine Writing <note>original: "Theographia"</note> wished to declare and explain the Deity to us through number for a threefold consideration. The first of these is to reveal His infinity, since nothing is more infinite than number, for there is no end to its magnitude. The second is to declare God as foreknowing; for number was (as the wise man says) undoubtedly the primary model in the mind of the Creator for the things to be created. The last is to indicate that God is immutable; for nothing is more unchangeable than the **One** <note>The mathematical unit or "Monad"</note> and its properties, as was said above. For the things that were, they are the same; the things that are, they were the same, and always shall be. Number, therefore, suggests that God is simple while being immutable; it suggests He is wise while being foreknowing; it suggests He is incomprehensible while being infinite; and finally, it suggests He is wonderful and singular through these three qualities.

Theologians chose the number **three** <note>the triad</note> above all others because they wished to show that God is the primary form of all things. That this is the principle of forms and the first and supreme root of physical bodies is taught to us by a most evident geometric demonstration. For if we consider that triangular figure with diligent intuition, we will perceive that it cannot be broken down <note>resolved</note> into others, nor is it subject to any prior principles, insofar as it is itself the principle for the composition of all other figures, and the end-point for their dissolution. For the square, the pentagon, and all other figures proceed from the triangle and return to it. Insofar as this surface is the principle of all linear things, it is necessary that all other surfaces, as well as the bodies constructed from those surfaces, are derived from it; and in their dissolution, it will again be necessary that they return to that triangular surface. Such, therefore, is God: from whom all things come, and in whom all things are folded together in a simplicity of resolution. Finally, whatever exists receives its "being what it is" from form, and not from matter; even matter itself receives its existence from form, while form itself is not susceptible to accidents <note>Form is the essential nature, while "accidents" are non-essential properties like color or weight</note>. From this fact—that the triad is the principle of forms—it suggests with wonderful and most secret truth the cause and principle of universality, which is alone and truly one, and incapable of being further divided. 

Furthermore, it is declared that this number **three** is most properly fitted to God alone because it is the most perfect number, completing all things. For it is beauty, perfecting the beginning, the middle, and the end, and having these parts equal and absolute; while on the contrary, the number **two** <note>the binary</note> walks along robbed of these three, having no beginning or end (because no middle point stands between them), and consequently it is destitute of this most holy gift of perfection. All other numbers, however many may possess a beginning, middle, and end, do not possess that perfection absolutely and simply, but only in a composite way. Thus, the number three reveals God: the principle, the cause, and the form from the primary Form; it reveals the most perfect being through the beginning, the middle, and the end; through the beginning, as He from whom all things come; through the middle, as He through whom all things are; and through the end, as He in whom all things reside. Furthermore, for this same reason—

TREATISE I. SECTION I. BOOK I.

by such a number, which in such a way is similar to such a relation, or is spoken of; in the Triad <note>original: "Triade," the number three or Trinity</note>, the monad <note>the number one or unity</note> is found as if by itself, and the dyad <note>the number two or duality</note> as if by itself; so also in the Trinity, the Dyad is as if by itself, such as the Father and the Son, and again, because the monad is by itself, such as the Holy Spirit. The Father and the Son, therefore, correspond to each other by relation, and not to the Spirit. The Spirit, as if by himself, is neither to be referred to the Father by name, nor to the Son. He is referred, therefore, by meaning, as the Spirit of the Breather is Spirit, and the Breather of the Spirit is Breather <note>This refers to the theological concept of "spiration," where the Holy Spirit "breathes" from the Father and Son</note>: the Breather is the Father and the Son, yet they are not two breathers, but one, and one spirit.

Finally, Divine Writing <note>original: "Theographia"</note> employs relational predication, wishing to demonstrate that **GOD** is in accord with himself—or rather, to indicate that He is harmony itself and a full and singular connection:
> *For whatever the Father does, these things the Son also does likewise, and one and the same Spirit works the same things, distributing to each as he wills.* <note>A synthesis of John 5:19 and 1 Corinthians 12:11</note>

An incomprehensible harmony and singular connection, so that many are one in the identity of person; indeed, the Deity of the persons is more plural than the primary unity of the Spirit and the Angelic; finally, it surpasses all sense. This is that which gives life to separate things, and which forces conflicting things into a union: which is to be understood from "relatives" <note>a term from logic referring to things defined by their relationship to another, like "father" and "son"</note>, which rejoice in mutual responsibility, and which use their relative predication for the sake of knowledge rather than separation, wishing **GOD** to be understood as invariable, to whom it is impossible for any change to succeed or approach; one majesty, one will, one operation of the three-in-one, with whom there is no transmutation of the "one" so that it ceases to be what it was, nor a shadow of turning, so that it stops now, and now returns to what it was. Finally, Theology accepts relative pronouncement, accepting **GOD** as invisible, uncircumscribed, not signifiable by name, nor comprehensible by intellect. For relative demonstrations do not define the thing at all, they do not compose a definition, and they do not declare the substance: thus "servant" and "master," "left" and "right," signify not *what* a thing is, but rather only *toward what* it is. Thus, there is no inference from relation to substance; it is not because the Father is God, and the Son is God, and the Holy Spirit is God, that there are therefore three Gods. The Father and Son, therefore, are predicated not in *what* they are, but in *toward what* they are, as is known: as the Father is father of the Son, and the Son as Son of the Father, and concerning the Spirit, as has been defined regarding him. Altogether, if they placed the relative distinction in a differing substance, it would seem to follow that if the Father is God, the Son is God, and the Holy Spirit is God, then there are three Gods, not one. They do not place this relation apart from God, so that many things may fittingly agree in one thing, nor do they make it differently, even if one of them were taken away from the other. Therefore, the name of Father is separated from the Son, and Master from Servant, and conversely the whole; and yet someone is at once Father and Son and Master and Servant, etc.

## CHAPTER XI.
### *How the square and the cube are found in the sacred Trinity of the supersubstantial nature.*

Concerning the number of the sacrosanct ternary <note>the number three</note> of the Deity, which is the simplest, most perfect, most absolute, and most fundamental of all, we have treated above at length, though in unrefined speech. There, we declared the holy number (claiming for itself the place after unity before all other numbers) to be so joined to the highest unity that it is not a mere duality (which is estimated in itself to be a most imperfect number, since it is a confusion of units, as the Pythagoreans <note>Followers of the Greek philosopher Pythagoras who believed numbers were the essence of all things</note> maintain), but also a trinity and a unity, insofar as it is a middle ground, participating in both the most perfect and most complete extremes. For what is more absolute than unity? What is more complete than the number three? Since unity is never moved outside its own nature, and the trinity...

Formal multiplication <note>In this context, "formal" refers to the "form" or spiritual blueprint of a thing, rather than its physical substance.</note> begins from the center of the base of the material pyramid; from there, it signifies the proportions of material dissolution, by which, as we recede from multitude, we may rise toward the yoke of unity. Therefore, the third <note>meaning the highest/outermost</note> heaven is the height and length of composed things, the middle is their breadth, and the lowest is their depth. These three, by their ineffable disposition, looking downward from outside their supersubstantial world and leaping forth into the material world in most pleasant harmony—expanding in a marvelous way through the whole of matter—have executed their threefold operation within it. Wherefore all things were produced from nothing in number, measure, and weight.

## CHAPTER XIII.

### Concerning the number seven, and what mysteries are
### contained within it.

The number seven results from the unity, the number two, and the number four, from which is born the *Diapason* <note>original: "Diapason"; the musical interval of an octave, considered a symbol of perfect harmony</note>, which is the most perfect harmony. By the power and proportion of this harmony, God descends from His immortal and purely formal throne into the universal orb of the material world, giving form and composition to all things. For this reason, this number was powerful and effective in the mystery of creation and was concerned with holy things; it is called the *number of rest*. For the seventh day was the Sabbath day. It is also called the *number of perfection*, because beyond the harmony of the octave (which consists of seven intervals), there is no transition for simple elements in harmony. Likewise, it is the number of *blessing and beatitude*; as the Poet says: *O thrice and four times blessed, etc.* <note>original: "O terque, quaterque beatus"; a reference to Virgil's Aeneid</note>. Furthermore, the formless matter of the world is made blessed by the perfection of this harmony. 

The Pythagoreans also called this the *number of virginity*, because it is a prime number, in that it is neither generated by others [within the first ten numbers] nor does it generate others; nor can it be divided into two equal parts. Furthermore, it is called the *number of the oath*; thus Abraham, when he made a covenant with Abimelech, set out seven lambs as a testimony. It is also the *number of health and cleansing from impure diseases*. Thus the Prophet Elisha said to Naaman the leper: *Go, and wash seven times in the Jordan.* Moreover, it is called the *number of holiness and praise*, whereof the Prophet said: *Seven times a day I have spoken praise to you.* It is also called the *number of vengeance and punishment*, as it is written: *Vengeance shall be given sevenfold for Cain*, and elsewhere: *Cain shall be punished sevenfold.* and again: *He who kills Cain shall pay sevenfold vengeance.* 

Furthermore, it is the *number of the salvation of worlds*; for sevens of all clean animals were brought into the Ark of Noah. It is the *number of servitude*, as Jacob served seven years for Leah. It is the *number of destruction and ruin*, as on the seventh day, all the fountains of the abyss being broken, the water flooded over the lands. It is the *number of mourning*, as the people mourned for Israel [Jacob] for seven days, etc. It is the *critical number observed by all Physicians*, as in: *And at the seventh hour the fever left the nobleman's son.* Infinite other observations can be devised concerning this hidden and mystical number, all of which would be as laborious for me to express here as they would perhaps be tedious for the reader; I shall leave aside the *number of the planets, the climacteric years, the seven ages, the seven metals*, and countless other things. 

And the reason (unless I am mistaken) for all these properties of the number seven—why it is employed for both good and evil—is because this number participates in the nature of light, form, perfection, and purity, insofar as the first part of its composition is the number three; and it participates partly in the nature of the matter of darkness, since its latter number, namely four, is the number of imperfection and impurity. Therefore, this number is both the author of life and composition, and the author of death and dissolution; specifically because it is composed of the first odd number, namely the number three (representing life), and the first even number, namely four. For the number two is not called a "number" by the Pythagoreans, but a "confusion of unities" <note>Pythagoreans viewed 2 as the principle of duality or division rather than a stable "number."</note>. From the odd, therefore, as if from the active (that is, form), and from the even, as if from the passive (that is, ma-

...from matter, all things are generated, and by the same path they are dissolved; but generation and life are a supernatural light and a harmonizing force, while corruption belongs to the lower regions and to the night and the tearing darkness. In his right hand is piety, kindness, and beneficence; in his left is severe punishment. They call him *Phoebus*, *Apollo*, and the *Sun*, whom they say carries the *Graces* <note>original: "Gratias & Charites"</note> in his right hand and a bow and arrows in his left. At night, they named him *Dionysus*, the one who mangles and tears apart, breaking himself into seven parts; but during the day, they named him *Apollo*, the one who recomposes those things which he had torn apart at night, and divides them again into seven parts. In the night, therefore, he breaks and tears asunder, and in the day he unites things, as if driving away evils. For this reason, he is called *Alexicacos* <note>original: "Alexicacos", from the Greek Ἀλεξίκακος, meaning "Averter of Evils"</note> by the Athenians, and by *Homer* he is called the author of health <note>original: "ὑγιῶν" (hygiōn)</note>. With these ideas, the opinion of the *Pythagoreans* also seems to agree, for they enclosed the world and the soul within seven limits. In the *first* place, they put unity, as the highest level of the soul and mind, through which the soul contains the supreme unity in the Creator and is made one and the same with Him; for all things pre-existing in the *Word* <note>original: "Verbo"</note> were one with that *Word*, according to the <term>Theologians</term>. The *second place* (containing a double proportion compared to the first) denotes the progress of the soul or mind with God. The *third* demonstrates the entry into itself, and thus is described the emergence of the persons of the Trinity—namely, one into another and the return of the third again into unity. But now we come to the sending of the Spirit of the Lord into the imperfect mass <note>The "massa imperfecta" refers to the unformed primeval chaos.</note>, and so we proceed to the number four. The *fourth* signifies the exit which the soul makes from itself, so that it may be occupied with things to be created, which are still unformed. And thus in the fifth, sixth, and seventh (which two final limits or places consist of solid numbers), it denotes the conversion of the bodies to which the soul is joined. I say *bodies*, for the world consists of a double body: namely, the incorruptible and celestial, and the corruptible and elementary. So also man, to retain the perfect image of the world, was made—according to the *Platonists*—of a double body: one elementary, the other celestial. The elementary is represented by the <term>cube</term> or solid of the number two <note>2 cubed, or 8</note>, which signifies matter, and the celestial by the cube of the number three <note>3 cubed, or 27</note>; which cube we said above was rather a surface or a square number, for the reasons we gave there. For although the spiritual elements are in themselves "moist bodies" <note>A term from Hermetic philosophy referring to the fluid nature of the celestial spheres.</note>, yet if ether, air, and fire are compared to solid bodies, they relate to them as a surface to a body, or as a square to a cube.

And Abraham breathed his last, and died in a good old age, an old man, and full of years, etc.*** From this it is clear that this number of solar revolutions produces an advanced age, a happy senescence, and a fullness of days. From this it is evident that there is an infinite mystery in the consideration of this septenary number. Indeed, I myself knew a most learned man who, by the power of this septenary number and with the assistance of a certain kind of oracle, did not hesitate to resolve doubtful and uncertain questions, and even promised to divine in some way concerning hidden matters, both present and future.

->CAP. XV.<-
->*On the mystery of divine numbers in creation.*<-

We mentioned above that simple numbers, or digits, refer to the supernatural essence and pertain to the super-celestial region, which is indeed infinite. Here, however, we have proposed to treat the divine reason of the quinary <note>the number five</note>, and then finally the denary <note>the number ten</note> number. Truly, as we demonstrated above that the monad <term>monad: the number one, representing unity or God</term> or unity is the source and origin of all numbers—from which the Dyas <term>dyas: the number two, or duality</term> is derived, not as a number but as a confusion of unities, insofar as it contains "one" within itself twice—we have therefore called it the principle of the imperfect number. This is because it possesses a beginning and a middle, yet lacks an end. This is unlike the ternary <note>the number three</note> number, which we have called the beginning of the perfect number, insofar as it has within itself a beginning, a middle, and an end, and is therefore held among the numbers of perfection. Thus we have said that in respect to these three terms—namely 1, 2, and 3—there is a relation through all other numbers proceeding into infinity. Just as unity is the root of the first perfect number, namely the ternary, which signifies universal form (for what does it matter if God is like unity, and the universal spirit is in potentiality like duality, if that spirit is not informed and actuated by that God, so that duality is finally perfected into a Trinity?), so also duality is the root of the imperfect quaternary <note>the number four</note> number, and of those which arise from it. And hence it is that, just as 3 relates to 1, so in the same proportion 5 relates to 3, and 7 to 5, and 9 to 7. Similarly, as one relates to 2, so 4 relates to 2, and 6 to 4, and 8 to 6; according to which simple progressions all other composite numbers are drawn out, but their perfection is unity. Therefore, just as imperfection arises from unity in the middle movement, so by its addition at the end, the third term is brought forth, from which the first of the perfect numbers arises: the ternary. From this it is clear that both imperfection and perfection—that is, both evil (in terms of us) and good—flow from the hands of God or Unity, in whose power lies that which is evil...

This is explained most excellently by that miraculous word, the **Tetragrammaton** <note>The four-letter Hebrew name of God, YHWH</note>, consisting of ***Yod, He,*** and ***Vav, He***; where the breathing of the ***He*** denotes the procession of the spirit in both, and seems to conjoin the ***Vav*** with the ***Yod*** on the right, and again the ***Yod*** with the ***Vav*** toward the right. For this reason, it must be understood that the middle of any number refers to the son and the center, because the middle of a number is always understood to be in odd and perfect numbers: Thus in the ternary <note>The number three</note> number there is duality, in the quinary <note>The number five</note> there is trinity, in the septenary <note>The number seven</note> there is quarternity, and in the novenary <note>The number nine</note> there is the quinary, which is also the exact middle (insofar as the middle is considered in even numbers) of the denary <note>The number ten</note> number, through which God, descending downward from his **superformal** <note>Beyond physical form</note> kingdom, immerses himself into confused matter, creating that thing from nothing and giving form to the shapeless by his own act and light.

Here, however, I would have you know that when we speak of the middle of an even number, we do not mean its center—which is plainly void and nothing—but its half-part: For the center of the **Dyad** <note>The number two</note> is nothing, because it has only two boundaries, but its half-part is 1. Likewise, the middle of the quaternary <note>The number four</note> number is two, but it lacks a center. And so it is in the others, such as 6, 8, and 10. From this it is clear that all perfection lies in odd numbers, where a center is found; as in 3, where 1 is the center, 1 is the boundary from which, and 1 is the boundary toward which. And in the quinary likewise, 1 is the center, 2 is one half-part, and 2 is the other; and in 7, 1 is the center, 3 the boundaries, etc. Therefore, in perfect simple things, unity is the boundary from which, trinity the boundary toward which, and duality the middle—but in such a way that this duality becomes unity. So also trinity is the boundary from which, and a trinity making six is the middle, and a trinity completing nine is the period; but here the center is superficial. Or trinity is the beginning, quinary the middle, and septenary the end; in the same way, quinary is the beginning, septenary the middle, and novenary the outcome. In all of these, the trinity of persons considered in the **supersubstantial** <note>Existing above all substance or matter</note> nature is found—that is, where form is totally regarded and not matter. And by this harmony GOD acted for the ordering of his **supereffential** kingdom in eternity, before he had decreed anything in his sacrosanct counsel concerning the creation of matter.

In this place, it must be observed that just as unity is the center of all forms, so too the ternary number becomes the first and nearest emanation of the divine majesty from its own nature toward the thing to be created; the quinary number is the second, the septenary the third, and the novenary the last. Thus there are five processes of the emanation of divine light: namely, the emission of the luminous form from unity toward 3, and from ternary toward 5, and from quinary toward 7, and from septenary toward 9, and from novenary toward 1—which number, by the addition of a cipher <note>A zero</note>, constitutes 10. From this it is clear that if GOD does not enter the abyss of matter, then he reflects his rays into himself, or into his own center and his own unity, according to that saying of ***Hermes Trismegistus: The Monad generates a monad and reflects its own heat back into itself.*** <note>original: *Mercur. # ON DIVINE NUMBERS:

Only he who has entered the field of the perfect binary <term>number two</term> could penetrate to the imperfect binary, which exists in potential toward something else. Thus, the supersubstantial <note>original: *supersubstantialis*; existing above or beyond physical substance</note> duality, by doubling itself, made the number seven <term>septenary</term> the middle; in this way, it joined perfection with imperfection in the first stage of procession from its super-heavenly nature to the mundane world. For the number four <term>quaternitas</term> is an even number and consequently imperfect, while the number three <term>ternarius</term> is a perfect number. Thus, from their first meeting, it is likely that matter or imperfection (represented by the number four) must be joined with perfection, insofar as the number three (attributed to form) is connected with it to complete the number seven.

Similarly, the number four is the "superficial" midpoint between two and six, denoting that the Word <note>The *Verbum* or the Second Person of the Trinity</note> is, as it were, the center of the operations of the six days of creation. Hence, after the heavens were established by the Word of the Lord on the fourth day, this King, giving form to his tabernacle, placed it on that day in the Sun. This fourth day, by dividing six into three dualities, was the superficial middle of the six days, or the essential center of the seventh day. For this reason also, the Sun, adorned with its own splendor, was placed in the middle of the world or the heavens. 

Similarly, the number four is half of the number eight <term>octonarius</term>, which signifies the "elemented" <note>the physical world composed of elements</note> or the cube, taking the half as it is reckoned among even numbers. For the number four is the square of the root 2. Thus, four represents the elements produced by the second person, from which the world is forged, and eight is the cube, from which the composition forged from those elements is made. Therefore, mundane duality—that is, the universal spirit—is truly imperfect, brought into the light from potentiality by the power of the uncreated duality (produced in the trinity of complete unity), from which the number four (the element) and the number eight (the elemented) arise. 

One proceeds further, therefore, from unity toward creation in this manner: The number five <term>quinarius</term> is the perfect midpoint between the number two and the number eight. It denotes, therefore, that the second person is in the middle between the universal Spirit and the elemented world, and consequently, that the Word is in us and in all composite things as a center, life, and essence. The number five is also the center of all the digits—namely, of the number nine—insofar as 1, 2, 3, and 4 are found on one side, and 6, 7, 8, and 9 on the other. 

Hence, he is also the center among the supersubstantial things: The Son is the center between the Father and the Spirit; he is the center in supersubstantial things; he is the center in things created and uncreated; he is the center of the uncreated Spirit and of the whole world, dwelling in the Sun; he is the center of the elements and the center of all elemented things. He is, therefore, the life of uncreated things; he is the life of the darkness; he is the life of the spirit or the created waters, holding his palace in the heart of the firmament. He is the life of the elements in the middle sphere of equality, sometimes appearing wonderfully in the center of the elements or the middle of the air. He is the life of elemented things, insofar as he is the essence and brilliance of wonders, the specific form of plants, and the being of animals, by which the life, reason, intellect, and mind of men breathe, insofar as he dwells in man abundantly. For, according to the witness of Paul, man's members *are the temple and palace of his own divinity.* 

Wherefore, by reason of the presence of this eternal Sun, man is called the **Microcosm** <note>original: *Microcofmus*; the "Little World," a common Renaissance concept that the human being is a miniature map of the entire universe</note>. And this was that Word of which Saint John makes mention, calling it the *life and light of every thing in this world, which the darkness did not comprehend, nor did the world know*; that *LET THERE BE* <note>original: *FIAT*</note>, *cited at the beginning of the first book [Genesis], by whose power every creature was made.* And in this way, the supersubstantial Dyad <term>the number two</term>, overflowing with uncreated spirit, progressed as far as the threshold or vestibule for entering **Hyle** <note>original: *hylam*; a Greek term for primordial, unformed matter</note>, namely to the number ten. This Dyad was divided by divine unity into the number two so that the uncreated unity itself, being present, might make man—who was created out of nothing as one—into something double: namely, God and man.

### CHAPTER XVI.
#### On the admirable mysteries of the numbers five and ten.

From what has been said, it clearly appears that the number <term>five</term> <note>original: *quinarius*</note> is the center of the number <term>ten</term> <note>original: *denarius*</note>, in which unity doubles itself or repeats itself beyond the limit of simplicity. Just as duality was the first midpoint of the number three (the boundary between 1 and 2, where both boundaries are odd and consequently perfect), so it is in the first number of composition, or the first "article," where divine unity joins itself with the cipher <note>the zero</note> or unformed matter—namely, in the number 10. There, the number five is found to be the center (speaking loosely) and the middle between 1 and 10. 

A great mystery is revealed therein: just as in the earlier terms 1, 2, and 3, the "two" is perfected by what comes before and after it because of the perfection of unity and trinity (for nothing except perfection exists in the super-heavenly kingdom), so it is in the terms 1, 5, and 10. In these, unity progresses through duality—or <term>GOD</term> through the Word—toward the creation of 5. This number 5, which is the middle number, is found between its origin (1) and the number 10. Because 10 is an even number, it denotes the imperfection of the matter to be created; therefore, its middle or center, which must be its life, is a perfect number, so that by its perfection, the matter may be made perfect. We ought to note that just as <note>original: אל</note> *El* is one name of God, denoting that He is the first of the <term>digits</term><note>In historical arithmetic, "digits" are the single numbers 1–9, while "articles" are the tens (10, 20, etc.)</note> and the unity of uncreated beings, so also <note>original: יה</note> *Jah* is another of His names, designating the end of the digits and the beginning of the <term>articles</term>, that is, the starting point of all created things composed of form and matter. And that <note>original: י</note> Jod is the first unity of the digits, and <note>original: י</note> Jod is the second unity, or the first of the articles, which follows that unity of the digits in the order of emanation; the order of the Holy Scriptures seems to hint at and acknowledge this, since it has been observed by the Kabbalists that <note>original: אלהים</note> Elohim is repeated 32 times in the creation before reaching the name <note>original: יהוה</note> Jehovah. For the name *El* begins with the letter <note>original: א</note> Aleph, which designates the beginning and unity, and the name *Jah* begins with <note>original: י</note> Jod, which equals 10—a number which is the end of all things. # OF THE FIRST TREATISE,
## SECTION I.
### B O O K II.
#### On divine harmony.
##### C H A P T E R I.
###### *On divine harmony & simple consonances.*

<image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial 'V' depicting a pastoral landscape with a shepherd standing with a crook amidst a flock of sheep, with mountains and a city in the background.</image-desc>

Just as material numbers in themselves produce nothing at all except discord and dissonance in the material world, so also the <term>essential and simple numbers</term><note>Also called "formal numbers," these are the ideal archetypes in the divine mind, as opposed to numbers used for counting physical objects.</note> found in the formal world can undoubtedly propagate nothing except concord, union, and love, both in their own region and in the material sphere. But in its immense kingdom, this divine harmony is heard with ineffable and incomprehensible joy and gladness, without any obstacle or hindrance of discord (which entered the material world from the beginning along with strife). In the world, however, this harmony acts, having been multiplied many times over, for the correction of contentious matter and the dissonances of darkness: Which is indeed demonstrated by the number of the Holy Trinity in this way. 

For the <term>monad</term><note>The number one, representing unity or God.</note> joined with the <term>dyad</term><note>The number two, representing the first step into multiplicity or the "other."</note> produces the <term>diatessaron</term><note>The musical interval of a perfect fourth, derived from the ratio 3:4 in Pythagorean theory.</note>, consisting of three intervals; yet there 4 voices are found, because the spirit is present there in the union of unity with duality; Thus the *Son* is said to be in the *Father*, and the *Father* with the *Son*, and the *Spirit with both*. Again, by the binding of duality with the number three, the <term>diapente</term><note>The musical interval of a perfect fifth, derived from the ratio 2:3.</note> will arise, since in such a number five voices are found constituting the diapente and four intervals (since it is only the addition of one tone, or a sounding person, to the diatessaron, which consists of three intervals.) For under this consonance the two first persons come together, and a double spirit proceeding from both. 

Therefore, that most exalted name, the <term>Tetragrammaton</term><note>The four-letter Hebrew name of God, YHWH (Yahweh). Fludd is mapping the letters to musical intervals.</note>, denotes these two consonances encompassed within the Trinity: namely *Yod He, and Vav He*, where the breath (*He*) denotes the Spirit proceeding from both. For that letter (*He*) being doubled ends both syllables and the whole name. It is pronounced, therefore, by these 4 letters as *Jova* <note>A Latinized form of the Tetragrammaton, often rendered as Jehovah.</note>; and in this way we have the two simpler consonances already open and manifest in the indivisible Trinity, from the union of which the <term>diapason</term><note>The musical interval of an octave. In classical theory, an octave is the combination of a perfect fourth and a perfect fifth.</note> is made, which is integrated from the diatessaron and the diapente. [fourth], when combined with a <term>fifth</term><note>Original: *diapente*. A musical interval encompassing five notes of the scale.</note>, the last note of the consonance of the fourth is the first note of the consonance of the fifth; and consequently, no more than eight notes are found in an <term>octave</term><note>Original: *diapason*. The interval spanning eight notes, considered the most perfect consonance.</note>. Finally, since the octave draws the efficacy of its consonance from the unison, its symphony is therefore connected with unity, from which it was numbered and derived. Again, if we proceed by way of proportions, we will find that unity and duality relate to one another in a double proportion (2:1), from which the octave is formed. And 2 to 3 exist in a <term>sesquialter proportion</term><note>A ratio of 3:2, which defines the musical interval of a fifth.</note>, of which the fifth consists. And 3 to the <term>Tetragrammaton</term><note>The four-letter Hebrew name of God (YHVH). Here Fludd uses it to represent the number four.</note>, or the conjunction of the Trinity with unity, denotes a <term>sesquitertian proportion</term><note>A ratio of 4:3, which defines the musical interval of a fourth.</note>, from which the fourth arises. Furthermore, if unity multiplied by itself brings forth the unison, duality multiplied by itself will bring forth the four notes of the consonance of the fourth. And again, 3 multiplied by 2, with unity added besides, will produce seven, denoting the intervals of that consonance called the octave; or by the addition of duality, its 8 notes will appear; or by the addition of 3, the number nine will leap forth, in which the notes of the fourth and fifth are encompassed.

Moreover, by proceeding in a retrograde way, 3 joined with unity denotes the four notes of the fourth, and 3 with duality, the five sounds of the fifth; if the Trinity is added to these, the eight notes of the octave will come forth. Whence it clearly appears that, in whatever way the persons of the Trinity are taken, they are always found in concord and symphony, and are observed to be immune from all discord and contrariety. For if we look at twice three, we find there also the fifth with a whole tone, completing that concord which musicians call the <term>sixth</term><note>In Fludd's system, the number 6 (2x3) represents the interval of a major or minor sixth.</note>; if finally the number three is multiplied by itself, it will produce a musical consonance, namely 9 notes fused and arising from the fifth and the fourth; since the consonance of the fourth is fused from 4 notes and the fifth from five, which added together are noticed to produce the most perfect consonance, the octave. The demonstration of this music follows here, insofar as it is found in the Trinity alone.

### CHAPTER II.

*How worldly harmony exists in the same manner as divine harmony, and how worldly and material symphony proceeds from that which is divine and formal.*

As the number ten <note>original: *denarius numerus*</note> relates to unity, so also does the harmony of the material world relate to that of the formal and <term>supersubstantial</term><note>Existing above or beyond the nature of physical substance; purely spiritual.</note> world. And just as unity was the beginning of the Music and concord of the Trinity, so also the number three <note>original: *ternarius*</note> multiplied by itself is the starting point of symphonic composition, because nine is the beginning of the number ten and the end of the simple numbers. Hence, for the formation and consonance of the material world, the Spirit of the Lord (who was the third person of the Trinity)—taking the place of unity within Himself as the Spirit of the Trinity—was carried over the waters, imparting to them a fiery love and a melody proceeding from that most holy harmony.

Therefore, the Spirit of Jehovah—with whom is the power of the Father (and consequently, supersubstantial unity), the wisdom of the Son (and consequently, supersubstantial duality), and the grace proper to Himself—this Spirit, I say, being three and one, is found in the number ten. Because He was now occupied with material composition, He claimed for Himself the place of unity in the universal and material essence. From Him flowed the second person, namely the **Sun**, whom **Plato** for this reason called the *visible son of God*; nor indeed did he wander far from the truth in this opinion since, as the royal Prophet <note>A reference to King David, traditionally considered the author of the Psalms.</note> testifies, *God placed his tabernacle in the sun*. The **Sun** is therefore like a second person in the material world, receiving his glowing and splendid virtue from the first person, or the fiery Spirit of God; it is seen to illuminate the waters of the middle region of the world, as well as the lowest, in the likeness of its Father (from whom it received its power), and it pours life into the lower things year by year.

The third person of the material world we call **man**, proceeding from the first and the second; hence **Hermes Trismegistus** says, *God is the light and life of man*, and another Philosopher teaches us that *the sun and man beget man*. **Hermes Trismegistus** also says in another place: *The world is the son of God, the sun is the son of the world, and man is the son of the sun.* But we understand "the world" as the universal essence of matter, which contains within itself three persons worthy of admiration (if it is permitted to compare substantial things with supersubstantial ones), just as the divine essence contains its own. But God is the life of the world, and the fiery and loving Spirit is esteemed as the first person of the world, from whom primarily the other two and all other things are derived. 

However, God is present to His simple and formal world in unity, but to the material world in the number ten, so that He might mingle Himself with the shapeless waters to give them form, and to drive away their dissonances and strifes by the symphony of His splendid countenance, binding the elements to one another in concordant peace by an inviolable bond of harmony. Since, therefore, the material world is merely a type and image of the <term>Archetype</term><note>The original divine model or "blueprint" of the universe in the mind of God.</note>, or supersubstantial world, we have derived this worldly Music of ours and the consonances of its every region or heaven from the observation of that divine harmony. 

First, therefore, we perceive with diligent insight that the unity of the Trinity joined with duality produces the consonance of the <term>fourth</term><note>original: *diatessaron*</note>, born from three intervals. Following this exemplar, we observe that the three hierarchies or regions of the <term>empyrean</term><note>The highest, most spiritual heaven, associated with pure light and fire.</note> heaven have produced in their arrangement a formula of melody not unlike this (by the breathing of the divine Spirit). Again, we perceive that, just as unity relates to duality in a double proportion (which constitutes the consonance of the <term>octave</term><note>original: *diapason*</note>), so in a similar way, the upper part of the pyramid of universal matter—or the first region, beginning from its cone or the beginning of the first heaven—relates to the intersection made by the two pyramids in the heart of heaven.
