# ON THE SPECULATION OF PYRAMIDAL SCIENCE

But now it must be understood of itself that these two combs, or these two hemispheres, must be so joined at the smallest points <note>original: *per minima*; referring to the smallest possible particles or points of contact</note> that those two parts of the same proportion constitute one and the same body. That is to say, there should be no empty gap between the teeth of the combs, but rather the empty and vacant spaces between the teeth of one comb are filled by the proper fit of the teeth of the other. For in this way, when the upper hemisphere enters into the nature of that lower hemisphere—which leaps forth from the earth for the sake of resistance—they coincide into one nature and identity of disposition, and they constitute one thing: namely, the universal spirit of the world, which **Moses and Peter** called "water." <note>Fludd identifies the "spirit of the world" with the primordial waters mentioned in Genesis and the Epistles of Peter.</note> For by the presence of the lucid and fiery spirit, infused into the dark spirit by the power of the Word, that Spirit—or universal water, or general moist nature—is purified and casts off its deformity, is rendered visible in part, and claims the name of "waters" for itself.

And because of the mixing of one nature with the other, that same spirit is sometimes called a "body"; sometimes the element of Earth, Water, Air, or Fire; sometimes Ether; and sometimes Light itself, according to whether there is a greater or lesser dominion of light within it. Thus, the higher the teeth of the material comb or hemisphere penetrate and ascend between the teeth of the formal <term>Formal: the "form" or active, shaping principle of a thing, associated here with divine light</term> hemisphere, the thicker and denser those sharp teeth find the other teeth of the formal hemisphere to be. And it is the same way, conversely, with the teeth of the formal hemisphere proceeding downward or descending between the teeth of the material hemisphere, as is plainly and evidently set before the eyes in the following figure *under Number 1.*

And although we have explained this demonstration of ours in a coarse manner, so that you, Good Reader, might more easily perceive our intention with your eyes and senses—namely, how the superior light penetrated into the lower material spirit that was overwhelmed by darkness before creation (for light penetrated into the dark spirit, and not the spirit into the light, lest in a backward way the passive should act upon the agent, and not vice versa)—nevertheless, I would have you consider even more deeply that the parts of light are mixed with the parts of the spirit at the smallest level between the teeth of the combs in that same proportion which has been declared. *For example:* in the following demonstration we have expressed two teeth of the combs, one of which will be of the formal comb, and the other of the material: We have divided these teeth into three or more parts, of which one part in one tooth corresponds to the other part of the other tooth in this manner:

*A. A. refers to the light and the Empyrean spirit, from which that heaven was made.* <term>Empyrean: the highest, most refined heaven composed of pure light and fire</term>

*B. B. has a relation to the proportion in the light and spirit of the ethereal heaven.* <term>Ethereal heaven: the middle region of the cosmos, containing the stars and planets</term>

*C. C. denotes the proportion between the light and spirit of the elementary heaven.* <term>Elementary heaven: the lowest, densest region of the world where the four elements (earth, water, air, fire) exist</term>

Let it be conceived, therefore, in the imagination, that the formal tooth is made of minium or red lead; but the tooth of the spirit is made of ceruse or white lead <note>Minium (red) and ceruse (white) were common pigments used to illustrate the mixing of active and passive substances</note>. Take then the portions of the two teeth A. <summary>Fludd explains how divine light and material spirit interlock like the teeth of two combs to create the universal "spirit of the world." ->TREATISE I. SECTION II. PART VII.<-

...will still claim for itself the name of **red lead** <note>original: *minium*; a bright red pigment made from lead tetroxide, used here to represent the dominant quality of light</note>. Thus, therefore, in the mixing at the smallest possible points <note>original: *per minima*; referring to the atomic or most fundamental level of intersection</note> of light—namely, of three portions of light with one part of spirit in the **Empyrean heaven**—that heaven possesses the name of the "light created on the first day." Conversely, in the portions of the teeth marked **C. C.**, a contrary arrangement is held: For a single part of **red lead** does not greatly change three parts of **white lead** <note>original: *cerussa*; a white pigment used to represent the dominant quality of matter or darkness</note>. Hence, the name of **white lead** remains there because of the predominance of that substance. In a similar way, because of the scarcity of light in the lowest heaven, the spirit is changed very little from its bodily nature, so that it is called "corporeal" <note>having a physical body or substance</note>, as much in water, air, and fire as in the earth itself.

From these things, therefore, we conclude that the **Metaphysical Pyramid** as well as the **Physical Pyramid** are mixed together precisely in this manner, so that both the aforementioned simple hemispheres constitute a single hemisphere created from matter and form—or spirit and light. And this same principle is to be understood regarding the whole sphere or **worldly orb**.

*See figure Number 2.*

From this core, numerous straight rays and wavy lines emanate outwards, overlaid on a geometric grid of concentric arcs and radial lines, suggesting a mathematical projection of light and its physical influence.]<-

### ON THE SPECULATION OF PYRAMIDAL SCIENCE.

This, therefore, is the aim of our intention, *kind Reader*, whenever we make any mention of the **formal** <note>The pyramid of light, representing divine influence and form</note> or **material pyramid** <note>The pyramid of shadow, representing physical substance and potentiality</note>; which I have wished to explain fully to you and others in this place for this reason: because it is the principal **key** or **gate** <note>original: *clavis sive porta*</note> of our doctrine, through which access lies open into the field of this Philosophy—indeed, truly into all true **natural science** <note>original: *scientia naturalis*; the study of the physical world and its governing laws</note>. But since few have been able to reach the **secret mystery** <note>original: *secretum mysterium*</note> of the **composition of the heavens**, due to a lack or the difficulty of a true understanding of these pyramids, I have therefore wished to treat them precisely and succinctly in this small book, so that those who desire this science may be able to reach the happy end and goal of their desire and honest wish by a much more ready and suitable path.

->THE END.<-
